initiative.title: Taskset Board Evidence And Performance IA
initiative.summary: Continue the UI/UX improvement loop after the TSAW refinement by using a lead-designer seminar to address evidence-gap overload, state-build latency, and performance-aware Taskset Board information architecture before the next source mutation.

taskset.display_name: Taskset Board Evidence And Performance IA
taskset.summary: Run a seminar-led UI/UX cycle for evidence-gap overload and performance-aware Taskset Board IA, publish an RFC, then derive the next implementation plus beta-evaluation registration.

tasks.title: Run Taskset Board evidence and performance IA seminar
tasks.goal: Create a lead-designer seminar artifact that chooses the next Taskset Board IA direction for high evidence-gap counts, slow state loading, and inactive-view layout containment without guessing the implementation before design review.
tasks.scope: Planning and evidence only. Do not edit UI source files. The seminar must cover typography, size and spacing, color and non-color cues, motion, effects, schema, assets, accessibility, responsiveness, interaction recovery, and state-loading budget.
acceptance: reviews/SEMINAR-2026-06-19-taskset-board-evidence-performance-ia.md records lead-designer, design-system-steward, interface-designer, ux-evaluator, and beta-tester viewpoints.
The seminar uses TASK-AR-615 evidence as input: evidence_gaps=49, live /api/tasksets_board latency watch, and inactive-view wide-child scan noise.
The seminar compares at least three directions: stale-evidence grouping, progressive disclosure with lane cap disclosure, and performance-split board loading.
The selected candidate states design_token, ui_component, pattern_component, and one_off_for_now implications before any implementation task is created.

The seminar defines evidence requirements for font scale, density, color, animation, focus/effects, schema contracts, assets, accessibility, responsive behavior, beta-tester interaction paths, and API latency.

units.title: Run evidence overload and performance IA lead-designer seminar
units.context: TASK-AR-615 closed BTC-TSAW-CLAIM-001 and BTC-TSAW-EMPTY-001, but its beta/UX evidence recommended a broader lead-designer cycle for evidence-gap overload, state-build latency, and performance-aware Taskset Board IA.
units.scope: Write the seminar decision artifact and refresh the evidence index only. Do not patch design docs or UI source files in this unit.
steps: Read the TASK-AR-615 beta, UX, and W4B evidence.
Record positions from lead-designer, design-system-steward, interface-designer, ux-evaluator, and beta-tester.
Compare stale-evidence grouping, lane cap disclosure/progressive drill-in, and performance-split board loading.
Choose one RFC candidate and explicitly reject weaker alternatives.
Classify expected reusable surfaces as design_token, ui_component, pattern_component, or one_off_for_now.
Define beta-tester evidence paths and gate commands for the RFC and next implementation taskset.
Refresh evidence index and run the recorded verification commands.
acceptance: The seminar is specific enough for a planner to write the RFC task without chat context.
Every UI quality dimension has concrete evidence expectations and an assetization class.
The chosen direction has explicit implementation boundaries, schema expectations, latency expectations, and a beta-tester follow-up path.
No UI source files are changed by this unit.
units.handoff: Report the selected Taskset Board evidence/performance IA direction, rejected alternatives, assetization implications, RFC target files, and next beta/UX evidence path.
units.stop_condition: Stop after seminar evidence is complete and ready for independent verification or RFC claim.

tasks.title: Publish Taskset Board evidence and performance IA RFC
tasks.goal: Promote the seminar decision into an accepted design-direction RFC that names the exact IA, visual, token, component, pattern, schema, loading-budget, and beta-evidence boundaries allowed for the next implementation round.
tasks.scope: RFC and accepted design-system documentation only. Do not edit UI source files. Update DESIGN.md or DESIGN-SYSTEM.md only for promoted reusable rules or asset contracts.
acceptance: reviews/RFC-2026-06-19-taskset-board-evidence-performance-ia.md states the selected IA/visual direction, target workflow, references, rejected alternatives, risks, and promotion decision.
The RFC defines typography, density, color/non-color state, motion, effects/focus, schema, assets, accessibility, responsiveness, interaction, and latency requirements for the next implementation.
The RFC lists minimum design-token, UI-component, pattern-component, and one-off boundaries before implementation.
DESIGN.md and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md are updated only when the RFC promotes a reusable rule or asset contract.
The RFC defines beta-tester and UX-evaluator evidence for the next implementation round.

tasks.title: Derive Taskset Board evidence and performance implementation units
tasks.goal: Turn the accepted evidence/performance IA RFC into a source-mutation implementation registration input and a paired beta/UX evaluation plan without bypassing W0-W6.
tasks.scope: Planning and registration input only. Do not edit UI source files. The output must be specific enough for interface-designer and ux-evaluator claims.
acceptance: A follow-up registration input names the next UI source mutation task, target files, target API/schema contracts, and token/component/pattern/one-off classification.
A beta-tester artifact plan records clicked/typed flows, recovery attempts, viewport/data state, keyboard traversal, reduced-motion behavior, API latency observation, and BTC-style failure routing.
The next implementation task keeps page files focused on layout and data wiring while repeated surface area is moved into pattern assets.
The plan preserves design-system gate, focused UI tests, evidence index, and independent W4b verification commands.
